item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. SCOPe places the transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, fumarate-reductase respiratory-complex transmembrane subunits, and respiratory nitrate-reductase gamma chains in the same heme-binding four-helical-bundle fold (f.21), but in separate superfamilies (f.21.1, f.21.2, and f.21.3, respectively). Sharing a fold records architectural similarity, not the probable common ancestry asserted at superfamily level. Thus SCOPe does not support treating all three as one homologous superfamily. Homology or detailed function should not be transferred among them solely from the four-helix/heme arrangement; templates may support only coarse fold, topology, or heme-geometry hypotheses unless sequence, ligand, and complex-context evidence independently supports a closer relationship. Representative structures should likewise be selected separately for each superfamily.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
